name: Adversarial NLI (ANLI)
description: We introduce a new large-scale NLI benchmark dataset, collected via an iterative, adversarial human-and-model-in-the-loop procedure. We show that training models on this new dataset leads to state-of-the-art performance on a variety of popular NLI benchmarks, while posing a more difficult challenge with its new test set. Our analysis sheds light on the shortcomings of current state-of-theart models, and shows that non-expert annotators are successful at finding their weaknesses. The data collection method can be applied in a never-ending learning scenario, becoming a moving target for NLU, rather than a static benchmark that will quickly saturate.
notes: Adversarially collected NLI dataset (human-and-model-in-the-loop) that is intentionally more difficult than static NLI benchmarks; risk of contamination from models used during collection; designed as a moving target rather than a saturating benchmark.
